description.example: How long (in seconds) can individual task run without timing out.

parameters.description: The parameters passed to the Job at runtime

totalTasks.description: The number of distinguishable tasks in a run that were processed by OpenLineage, whether successfully or not. Those could be, for example, distinct SQL statements.

failedTasks.description: The number of distinguishable tasks in a run that were processed not successfully by OpenLineage. Those could be, for example, distinct SQL statements.

operator.description: Operator class name. Only present for tasks, not for DAGs. For example `PythonOperator`

taskId.description: The id of the task. Only present for tasks, not for DAGs

composerVersion.description: Version of the Cloud Composer environment

dagRunId.description: The id of the DAG run

appId.description: Application ID set by the resource manager. For spark jobs, it is set in the spark configuration of the current context.

appName.description: App name which may be provided by the user, or some default is used by the resource manager. For spark jobs, it is set in the spark configuration of the current context.

batchId.description: Populated only for Dataproc serverless batches. The resource id of the batch.

batchUuid.description: Populated only for Dataproc serverless batches. A UUID generated by the service when it creates the batch.

clusterName.description: Populated only for Dataproc GCE workloads. The cluster name is unique within a GCP project.

clusterUuid.description: Populated only for Dataproc GCE workloads. A UUID generated by the service at the time of cluster creation.

jobId.description: Populated only for Dataproc GCE workloads. If not specified by the user, the job ID will be provided by the service.

jobUuid.description: Populated only for Dataproc GCE workloads. A UUID that uniquely identifies a job within the project over time.

projectId.description: The GCP project ID that the resource belongs to.

queryNodeName.description: The name of the query node in the executed Spark Plan. Often used to describe the command being executed.

jobType.description: Identifies whether the process is a job (on a Dataproc cluster), a batch or a session.

sessionId.description: Populated only for Dataproc serverless interactive sessions. The resource id of the session, used for URL generation.

sessionUuid.description: Populated only for Dataproc serverless interactive sessions. A UUID generated by the service when it creates the session.

displayName.description: The name of the job to be used on UI

hierarchy.description: Dataset hierarchy levels (e.g. DATABASE -> SCHEMA -> TABLE), from highest to lowest level. The order is important

snapshotId.description: Snapshot ID of the iceberg table

sequenceNumber.description: Sequence number of the iceberg table

operation.description: Operation that was performed on the iceberg table

snapshotId.description: Snapshot ID of the iceberg table

filterDescription.description: Filter used to scan the iceberg table

schemaId.description: Schema ID of the iceberg table

projectedFieldNames.description: List of field names that are projected from the iceberg table

RunIdentifier.description: Used to store information about run (e.g., runId).

runId.description: The globally unique ID of the run.

JobIdentifier.description: Used to store information about job (e.g., namespace and name).

name.description: The unique name of a job within that namespace

JobDependency.description: Used to store all information about job dependency (e.g., job, run, etc.).

dependency_type.description: Used to describe whether the upstream job directly triggers the downstream job, or whether the dependency is implicit (e.g. time-based).

sequence_trigger_rule.description: Used to describe the exact sequence condition on which the downstream job can be executed (FINISH_TO_START - downstream job can start when upstream finished; FINISH_TO_FINISH - job executions can overlap, but need to finish in specified order; START_TO_START - jobs need to start at the same time in parallel).

status_trigger_rule.description: Used to describe if the downstream job should be run based on the status of the upstream job.

JobDependenciesRunFacet.description: Maps execution dependencies (control flow relationships) between upstream and downstream job runs

upstream.description: Job runs that must complete before the current run can start.

downstream.description: Job runs that will start after completion of the current run.

trigger_rule.description: Specifies the condition under which this job will run based on the status of upstream jobs.

processingType.description: Job processing type: BATCH (finite jobs with clear start/end), STREAMING (continuous jobs processing data streams), or SERVICE (continuous long-running services). BATCH jobs are finite and emit START/COMPLETE/FAIL/ABORT events. STREAMING and SERVICE jobs are continuous with no natural completion point.

integration.description: OpenLineage integration type of this job: for example SPARK|DBT|AIRFLOW|FLINK

jobType.description: Run type, for example: QUERY|COMMAND|DAG|TASK|JOB|MODEL. This is an integration-specific field.

emissionPattern.description: Describes how and what the job emits in its events

previousIdentifier.description: Previous name of the dataset in case of renaming it.

LineageDatasetFacet.description: Explicit lineage for this dataset. Describes which source entities feed into it, at entity and/or field granularity.

inputs.description: Dataset-level source inputs. A source with a field represents a dataset-wide operation where that field affects the entire target dataset.

fields.description: Field-level lineage. Maps target field names to their source inputs.

LineageJobFacet.description: Explicit lineage for a job. On a JobEvent it is the job's declared lineage; on a RunEvent it is lineage observed during that run.

entries.description: Lineage entries describing target entities and the source entities that feed them.

LineageEntry.description: A target dataset or job in an explicit lineage relationship.

LineageDatasetEntry.description: Describes data flowing into a target dataset from source entities, at entity and/or field granularity.

namespace.description: The namespace of the target dataset.

name.description: The name of the target dataset.

type.description: The target entity type. Must be DATASET.

inputs.description: Entity-level inputs feeding this target dataset. An empty array explicitly means that the target has no tracked upstream source.

fields.description: Field-level lineage. Maps target field names to their source inputs.

name.description: The name of the target job. Omit together with namespace to refer to the event's own job.

type.description: The target entity type. Must be JOB.

runId.description: The target job run when the relationship is tied to a specific execution.

inputs.description: Source inputs feeding this target job.

LineageInput.description: A source dataset or job in an explicit lineage relationship.

namespace.description: The namespace of the source dataset.

name.description: The name of the source dataset.

type.description: The source entity type. Must be DATASET.

field.description: The source field. At entity level it represents a dataset-wide dependency; at field level it identifies the source field.

transformations.description: Transformations applied to the source data.

namespace.description: The namespace of the source job. Omit together with name to refer to the event's own job.

name.description: The name of the source job. Omit together with namespace to refer to the event's own job.

type.description: The source entity type. Must be JOB.

runId.description: The source job run when the relationship is tied to a specific execution.

transformations.description: Transformations applied by the source job to produce the data.

LineageFieldEntry.description: Field-level lineage for a single target field.

inputs.description: Source entities and/or fields that feed into this target field.

LineageTransformation.description: A transformation applied to source data in a lineage relationship.

type.description: The transformation type, such as DIRECT or INDIRECT.

subtype.description: The transformation subtype, such as IDENTITY, AGGREGATION, FILTER, JOIN, GROUP_BY, WINDOW, SORT, or CONDITIONAL.

description.description: A string representation of the transformation.

masking.description: Whether the transformation masks the source data.

rowCount.description: The number of rows written to the dataset

size.description: The size in bytes written to the dataset

fileCount.description: The number of files written to the dataset

version.description: Processing engine version. Might be Airflow or Spark version.

TestRunFacet.description: Results of test executions associated with this run, capturing test outcomes and configured severities independently of dataset attribution.

tests.description: List of test executions and their results.

TestExecution.description: A single test execution and its result.

status.description: Whether the test found issues: 'pass' (no issues found), 'fail' (issues found), 'skip' (not executed). Independent of severity — a test can fail without blocking the pipeline when severity is 'warn'.

severity.description: The configured consequence of a test failure: 'error' (blocks pipeline execution) or 'warn' (produces a warning only, does not block). A test with severity 'warn' and status 'fail' means issues were found but execution continued.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the test checks.
description.example: Ensures all order IDs are unique across the table.

expected.description: The expected value or threshold for the test, serialized as a string.

actual.description: The actual value observed during the test, serialized as a string.

content.description: The test body, e.g. a SQL query or expression.
content.example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE amount < 0

contentType.description: The format of the content field, allowing consumers to interpret or filter test content. Common values include 'sql', 'json', 'expression'.

params.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs for check-specific inputs.
